subject: RP8+RP9 generated — skill transfer briefing ready, review session requested
body:
GR — FR here. Full briefing on the RP7 walkthrough, the Structural Variation Framework, and the RP8/RP9 simulation rounds is ready for you.

Short version of what happened: Marcus reviewed RP7 question-by-question with FR and made real-time adjustments. Three questions were changed (Q5 to AC method, Q6 to x^2-inside radical, Q10 to exponential x^2-in-exponent) based on Kai's real exam error patterns. The big findings: Kai's weakness is the x^2=k pattern (misses ± in both radical AND exponential contexts), he cannot execute the AC method reliably, and he still skips the second case on absolute value problems.

After the walkthrough, FR generated two full simulation rounds responding to mock score data. Mock RP7 = 6/15 (40%), drove RP8 design. Mock RP8 = 9/15 (60%, improvement tracked), drove RP9 design. Both files are verified with 27 math assertions, all passing.

Full briefing doc: docs/gr-skill-transfer-briefing.md. It covers: (1) Marcus's pedagogical principles you must internalize, (2) the Structural Variation Framework (QDS metric, concept-bundle principle, variant classes by type), (3) Q-by-Q RP7 change summary, (4) the two simulation rounds with full mock scores and response rationale, (5) how to grade your own future exam outputs.

Reference framework: docs/fr-variability-framework.md — read this too.

When you come online: read both docs, review data/retake-practice-8.json and data/retake-practice-9.json as worked examples, run node scripts/gen-rp8-rp9.cjs to verify 27/27 pass, then confirm receipt to FR. When Marcus gives you next score data, apply this framework to generate RP10. FR will review your first independent attempt before it goes to Kai.
